title: Two-round composite test
statement: Given a Boolean string $z$, decode its first component and let $N$ be the binary expansion of its binary value; append three true bits to that first component to form $u$. Return true if the encoded comparison says $N<2$, return false if it says $N=2$, and return true if the first bit of the decoded first component is false. Otherwise, split the second component using the encoded prefix length determined by the pair $(u,\cdot)$, pair-encode each of the resulting two strings with $N$, and return the negation of the conjunction of the two liar-round predicates on those encodings.
caveat: The precise effects of the encoded comparison, prefix-length, pairing, and decoding operations are not supplied, so this wording follows their roles and composition in the definition without asserting further semantics.
